issue_context.title: Add Metrics overloads taking more tags
comments: I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

review_comments: Probably we should set the `_overflowTags` to null here too to unroot the memory. It's also more consistent with all the different implementations of the methods.

I am not seeing nulling the array pointer would be good if we already paid the cost of the memory allocation, why we need to repay it again after clearing the list? Please let me know if you think otherwise.

I do not foresee people reusing these very often to justify keeping the alloc around. That being said, the allocation is fairly small. If you think the allocation can be reused by using clear to avoid allocation for many tag use, that seems reasonable to me.

Think about when users want to clear the list? they will need to do that to reuse it for adding added items to it. Also, this list is defined as a struct, so it is expected any allocated memory lifetime will be short anyway. I am not seeing any concern keeping the allocated array when clearing the list.
minor: do we want this to be in `DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs` or a place agnostic to `Activity`?

I am not sure I understand the question here. The `System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs` is the source file containing all exposed interfaces in System.Duagnostics.DiagnosticSource to create the ref assembly. I am not sure why we need to have this in other place.
I was under the assumption that `DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs` is specific to the Activity class. If not, never mind.

The `Activity` class itself is defined in [System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/3374616f4412e10d70a7a943e81bbbedcfa4ec26/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSource/ref/System.Diagnostics.DiagnosticSourceActivity.cs#L9)
Should we use the same `goto case 7` that you've used in the other methods here?

We cannot do it here. The reason is we need to search the items in order, I hope the language can provide the capability doing something like:

case 8: 
       execute (go to 7;
       check Tag8
We shouldn't get here, but if this gets extended for more allocation-free tags and we forget this will get us. We should make this state an exception throw.
I hesitate to throw exception here because it wouldn't be right callers get exception for something not their fault. I'll add assert here instead. Thanks!
Yeah, it's not their fault but it doesn't leave them in a good state. I'm not strongly advocating for, but debug.assert would only happen on our tests.
Our tests covering such cases and we run debug builds in the CI. There where we catch such issues.
